canonical_name: Mittag-Leffler theorem for meromorphic functions (exact analytic variant open)
literal_source_claim_zh: 亚纯函数的部分分式分解
statement_blocker: The catalog supplies only a theorem name and a short decomposition gloss. It does not select prescribed-principal-parts existence versus decomposition of a given meromorphic function; fix the complex domain, discrete pole data, principal-part representation, local matching, convergence and correction terms, uniqueness boundary, ordered binders, or degenerate cases. Choosing a standard textbook form at intake would invent proposition-changing mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: an approved source must fix the complex plane, a connected open plane domain, an open Riemann surface, or another domain; the codomain, discrete or locally finite pole index type, principal-part data, and all universe and analytic structures.
conclusion: Open: existence of a meromorphic function with source-defined prescribed principal parts, or a source-defined partial-fraction decomposition of a given meromorphic function, with exact convergence, equality, and uniqueness clauses unresolved.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before a proposition is selected; the statement phase must resolve every case listed in scope-map.md.
candidate_scope_not_credited: on a source-selected plane domain, every locally finite family of finite principal parts is realized by a meromorphic function
every meromorphic function on a source-selected domain equals a source-convergent corrected sum of its principal parts plus a holomorphic function
solutions realizing identical principal parts differ by a holomorphic function
the whole-plane sequence formulation for poles tending to infinity
excluded_substitutions: finite polynomial or rational partial-fraction decomposition
finite-support divisor realization without arbitrary principal-part coefficients
Weierstrass factorization, Runge approximation, a Cousin problem, Laurent expansion, residue calculus, or meromorphic-order infrastructure alone
the category-theoretic Mittag-Leffler condition on inverse systems
a structure or hypothesis storing the desired result
the catalog's untrusted verified label or discovery probe as proof credit
